title: The Deterministic Horizon: When Extended Reasoning Fails and Tool Delegation Becomes Necessary
claim: Unaided step-by-step reasoning decays predictably with depth and crosses a failure threshold, while delegating to an external tool stays robust.
layout: 1 panel line plot, accuracy vs depth, dotted 50% line and dashed vertical marker
description: A single line plot with reasoning depth d (0 to 60) on the x-axis and accuracy in percent (0 to 100) on the y-axis. Orange circular markers with small error bars show empirical accuracy falling from about 88% at d=5 to about 10% at d=50. A blue dashed fitted-model curve runs through them, starting at 100% and decaying toward about 5%. A horizontal dotted gray line marks 50% accuracy. A vertical dashed gray line labeled d* crosses it at d≈22, where a blue dot marks the crossing. A green dashed line with small triangle markers, labeled Tool, stays high, declining gently from about 94% to 82%. The legend below lists Fitted model, Empirical and Tool. The eye goes first to the steep orange and blue decay and then to the flat green line above it.
caption: Accuracy versus reasoning depth on PermutationProbe. Neural CoT (Empirical, GPT-4o) tracks the functional form of Theorem 4.2 (Fitted model, dashed), crossing 50% (dotted) at the deterministic horizon d∗≈22; tool delegation (Tool, C3) declines only mildly, from 94% to 82%, across the same range. The curve is the bound of Theorem 4.2 evaluated at parameters fitted to these data (Appendix E) and is shown as a functional-form comparison, not an independently derived bound. Empirical markers are perdepth means ± std over 3 runs; Tool markers are six depth-bin means from Table 22.
abstract: Extended chain-of-thought reasoning can degrade performance on deterministic state-tracking tasks, not solely because of preference biases but, on the evidence we present, because of information-theoretic limits in the capacity of decoder-only attention. We present: (1) an Attention Bottleneck analysis providing evidence that total state-tracking capacity in bits is bounded in terms of head count, head dimension, and context length under stated modeling assumptions, and that total capacity is not the binding constraint; (2) a context-dependent error model with a depth-dependent quadratic term in the error exponent; (3) the State-Space Jaccard metric measuring state drift; and (4) a Deterministic Horizon $d^* \in [19, 31]$ (at $Î±= 0.5$) marking the depth at which unaided accuracy crosses 50%. Across twelve models and eight task domains (including SWE-Bench, WebArena, and SQL-Multi), tool-integrated reasoning reaches 76-94% accuracy versus 17-42% for neural chain-of-thought on PermutationProbe. Fine-tuning on optimal-length traces yields $<$3 percentage-point improvement, supporting an architectural ceiling.
